To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
reductive glutamine carboxylation is the major pathway for de novo lipogenic AcCoA synthesis in hypoxic and VHL-deficient cells, and is dependent upon the IDH1 enzyme.
IDH1-dependent reductive glutamine catabolism is the major source of acetyl-CoA and lipogenesis in hypoxic cells.
IDH1-mediated glutamine reductive metabolism is a major source of AcCoA for de novo lipids in hypoxic cells.

the reductive carboylation of glutamine is an important mechanism by which cancer cells can generate lipids for growth and survival.
the IDH1-mediated reductive metabolism of glutamine-derived alpha-ketoglutaric acid is a critical source of AcCoA for lipogenesis in hypoxic mammalian cells.

The main takeaway from our work is that

cells grown under hypoxic conditions rely almost exclusively on reductive glutamine to synthesize Acetyl-CoA for lipid synthesis, and that renal cell lines deficient for the VHL tumour suppressor use reductive glutaminolysis to synthesize Ac-CoA for lipid biosynthesis under normal culture conditions.
the metabolism of glutamine is not simply a means for generating amino acids and nitrogen, but is also a major route for generating AcCoA for de novo fatty acid biosynthesis.
the metabolism of glutamine is not just a source of carbon skeletons for amino acid biosynthesis, but it can also be an important carbon source for lipid biosynthesis.
